lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

hospital_abroad.description: Whether the child is in hospital abroad.

conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

Let me start with: **Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello, yes I'm inquiring about my child. I have one child - Alex, who's 3 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. So you have one child, Alex, who is 3 years old.

Now I need to ask: **Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great. Now I need to understand your relationship with Alex to determine responsibility.

**Do you live with Alex, or if not, do you contribute financially towards their upkeep (such as for food, clothes, or pocket money)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't live with me. But I do contribute towards their upkeep - I help out with things like clothes, food, and other essentials.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To determine if you qualify, I need to understand the amount you're contributing.

**How much do you contribute towards Alex's upkeep, and how often do you make these contributions (weekly, monthly, or as a lump sum)?** 

For reference, the current Child Benefit rate is £25.60 per week for the eldest or only child, which is about £110 per month. You would need to contribute at least this amount to qualify for Child Benefit when the child doesn't live with you.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I contribute £50 a week towards Alex's upkeep.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. Let me ask one more important question:

**Has anyone else (such as the person Alex lives with) already claimed Child Benefit for Alex?**

It's important to know because only one person can receive Child Benefit for the same child.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the person Alex lives with isn't claiming Child Benefit for them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:

- Alex is 3 years old, which meets the age requirement (under 16)
- You live in the UK
- Although Alex doesn't live with you, you're contributing £50 per week towards their upkeep (for clothes, food, and other essentials)
- This contribution exceeds the current Child Benefit rate of £25.60 per week for an eldest or only child
- According to the rules, you're considered responsible for a child if you're paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit towards looking after them
- No one else is currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex

Since you meet all the criteria, you can claim Child Benefit for Alex. You'll need to make a claim to start receiving the benefit.

**Please note:** If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may have to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge. However, you can still claim Child Benefit even if this applies to you.
